tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

JusPrin's UI sizes and colours live in one token file,
`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, which feeds the Agent pages (CSS
variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.

## Sources of truth

- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page
  `9:153`. Variables hold colours, spacing, radius, elevation and text styles;
  components hold control sizes.
- The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL.
  Its `tokens.json` was generated from Figma's variables and matched them

**What I checked**
- The worktree `JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign` is on `claude/composer-redesign` at `170d1ae080`. The uncommitted files match the handoff's list, and the worktree has its own `build/arm64` and `node_modules`.
- Both Figma spec files are in the local figma-mirror folder. The proposal spec was updated today.
- `design-system.md`, `fork-stewardship.md` and `handoff-design-token-sync.md` all exist.

**What's missing or unclear**
1. **The token sync has to come first, and it hasn't been done.** Step 1 says the composer can't use the Figma sizes until the shared design tokens are updated. Those are the tokens in `design-tokens.json` that every screen reads. My guess is the sync hasn't started: its handoff is still untracked and I found no token-sync branch or worktree. I haven't confirmed that with whoever owns it. The token-sync handoff also has its own open questions for you, such as what to do with colours that exist only in the code. So I need you to decide: do the sync here first, or wait for another session to do it.
2. **The provider, model and thinking-level pickers need a conversation with you first.** The handoff says so itself, so that's expected. Steps 2, 3 and 5 (focus ring, native file picker, build and screenshots) don't depend on anything else.
3. **One small ambiguity about the focus ring.** The artifact's `border-focus` token says "2px ring, offset 2px". The Composer component draws the 2px stroke on the box's own edge. I'd follow the Composer component unless you say otherwise.

**Getting into the artifact**
The handoff gives only the URL (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the bare filename `tokens.json`. That filename doesn't work as a path: reading it fails. The file is actually at `project/tokens.json`. I found that by listing the artifact's files with the Artifact tool, then read it. The token-sync handoff, unlike this one, also names a local copy at `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.

Two things to know about what's in the artifact:
- **`tokens.json` doesn't hold the control sizes this task needs.** It has colours, spacing, radius, shadows and five component sizes. The icon button's 32 px and the menu row's 36 px aren't in it. Those come from the Figma components, through the local spec files.
- **The artifact's Composer description is the old design.** It describes a 50 px entry with an "Attach a file" link, not the + menu. That fits the handoff's note that the artifacts haven't been re-synced, so the spec files are the current design source, not the artifact.

1	# Handoff: bring the code's design tokens in line with the design system
2	
3	JusPrin's UI sizes and colours live in one token file,
4	`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, which feeds the Agent pages (CSS
5	variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
6	in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
7	artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
8	truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
9	document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.
10	
11	## Sources of truth
12	
13	- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page
14	  `9:153`. Variables hold colours, spacing, radius, elevation and text styles;
15	  components hold control sizes.
16	- The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL.
17	  Its `tokens.json` was generated from Figma's variables and matched them
18	  exactly at the last sync (2026-10-13). A local copy is at
19	  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.
20	- Component sizes are not variables in Figma; they are the sizes of the
21	  components themselves. The table below was read from the local copy of the
22	  Design System page, `figma-mirror/figma/spec3/9-153.txt`. Note: the Composer
23	  component was rebuilt in Figma after that read and the new read is
24	  incomplete, so treat the Composer's numbers there as stale.
25	
26	## Differences found
27	
28	### Colours
29	
30	Light-mode values match. Three dark-mode status colours differ:
31	
32	| Token | Design system (dark) | Code (dark) |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| success | `#4CAF82` | `#58B894` (`primitive.successDark`) |
35	| danger | `#E07080` | `#F07A8E` |
36	| warning | `#E8B84A` | `#E9B960` |
37	
38	These colours exist only in the code, with no design-system counterpart:
39	`action.secondary`, `secondaryHover`, `secondaryPressed`, `secondaryText`,
40	`secondaryBorder`, `action.danger`, `dangerText`, `dangerBorder`,
41	`overlayScrim`, `statusSuccessOnAction`, `textOnAction`. Ask Kenneth whether
42	each should be added to Figma (then the artifact) or replaced by an existing
43	design-system colour. Do not delete them on your own.
44	
45	### Radius
46	
47	| Design system | Value | Code | Value |
48	|---|---|---|---|
49	| radius-small | 4 | `dimension.radius.standard` | 4 |
50	| radius-medium | 8 | `compact`, `container` | 8, 8 |
51	| radius-large | 12 | `window` | 12 |
52	| radius-chip | 4 | (no token; `component.chip.radius` 4) | 4 |
53	| radius-full | 10 | `pill` | 9999 |
54	
55	Values agree except `full` (10) vs `pill` (9999). Names differ throughout.
56	Decide with Kenneth whether to rename the code tokens to the design-system
57	names (touches every consumer and guard test) or keep the code names and only
58	fix the values. Renaming is cleaner but a larger diff.
59	
60	### Spacing, elevation, text styles
61	
62	Same in both. Nothing to do.
63	
64	### Control sizes (Figma component vs code token)
65	
66	| Component | Figma | Code token | Code value | Action |
67	|---|---|---|---|---|
68	| Button/Icon | 32x32, radius 4 | `component.button.icon` | 26x26 | change to 32 |
69	| Button/Primary | 34 high, padding 8/16, radius 8 | `button.primary` | padding 8/16, radius 8 | same; check the rendered height is 34 |
70	| Button/Secondary | 32 high, padding 6/12, radius 4 | `button.secondary` | padding 6/12 | same; check height 32 |
71	| Button/Link | 26 high, padding 0/4 | none found | | find what the code uses |
72	| Menu/Row | 36 high, full width, padding 8/12, gap 8, no radius | `menuRow` | 32 high, radius 4, side inset 4 | change, but see the warning below |
73	| Menu/Popover | 280 wide, padding 8 top/bottom, row gap 2, radius 8 | `popover` | padding 4, gap 0, radius 8 | change, but see the warning below |
74	| Chip/Printer+Spool | 28 high, radius 4 | `chip` | 26 high | change, but see the warning below |
75	| Chat/Reply Choice | 28 high, padding 0/12 | `replyChip` | 28, 12 | same |
76	| Field/Number, Select, Form Row | 26 high, radius 4 | `field`, `select`, `formRow` | 26 | same |

# Handoff: bring the code's design tokens in line with the design system

JusPrin's UI sizes and colours live in one token file,
`resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, which feeds the Agent pages (CSS
variables) and the native shell (`ShellTheme`). The design system itself lives
in the Figma file "JusPrin v2" and is mirrored, value for value, in a Claude
artifact. On 2026-10-19 Kenneth ruled that the design system is the source of
truth: where the token file disagrees with it, change the token file. This
document lists every known disagreement and what to do about each.

## Sources of truth

- Figma file "JusPrin v2", key `jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH`, Design System page
  `9:153`. Variables hold colours, spacing, radius, elevation and text styles;
  components hold control sizes.
- The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL.
  Its `tokens.json` was generated from Figma's variables and matched them
  exactly at the last sync (2026-10-13). A local copy is at
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/published/ds/project/tokens.json`.
- Component sizes are not variables in Figma; they are the sizes of the
  components themselves. The table below was read from the local copy of the
  Design System page, `figma-mirror/figma/spec3/9-153.txt`. Note: the Composer
  component was rebuilt in Figma after that read and the new read is
  incomplete, so treat the Composer's numbers there as stale.

## Differences found

### Colours

Light-mode values match. Three dark-mode status colours differ:

| Token | Design system (dark) | Code (dark) |
|---|---|---|
| success | `#4CAF82` | `#58B894` (`primitive.successDark`) |
| danger | `#E07080` | `#F07A8E` |
| warning | `#E8B84A` | `#E9B960` |

These colours exist only in the code, with no design-system counterpart:
`action.secondary`, `secondaryHover`, `secondaryPressed`, `secondaryText`,
`secondaryBorder`, `action.danger`, `dangerText`, `dangerBorder`,
`overlayScrim`, `statusSuccessOnAction`, `textOnAction`. Ask Kenneth whether
each should be added to Figma (then the artifact) or replaced by an existing
design-system colour. Do not delete them on your own.

### Radius

| Design system | Value | Code | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| radius-small | 4 | `dimension.radius.standard` | 4 |
| radius-medium | 8 | `compact`, `container` | 8, 8 |
| radius-large | 12 | `window` | 12 |
| radius-chip | 4 | (no token; `component.chip.radius` 4) | 4 |
| radius-full | 10 | `pill` | 9999 |

Values agree except `full` (10) vs `pill` (9999). Names differ throughout.
Decide with Kenneth whether to rename the code tokens to the design-system
names (touches every consumer and guard test) or keep the code names and only
fix the values. Renaming is cleaner but a larger diff.

### Spacing, elevation, text styles

Same in both. Nothing to do.

### Control sizes (Figma component vs code token)

| Component | Figma | Code token | Code value | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Button/Icon | 32x32, radius 4 | `component.button.icon` | 26x26 | change to 32 |
| Button/Primary | 34 high, padding 8/16, radius 8 | `button.primary` | padding 8/16, radius 8 | same; check the rendered height is 34 |
| Button/Secondary | 32 high, padding 6/12, radius 4 | `button.secondary` | padding 6/12 | same; check height 32 |
| Button/Link | 26 high, padding 0/4 | none found | | find what the code uses |
| Menu/Row | 36 high, full width, padding 8/12, gap 8, no radius | `menuRow` | 32 high, radius 4, side inset 4 | change, but see the warning below |
| Menu/Popover | 280 wide, padding 8 top/bottom, row gap 2, radius 8 | `popover` | padding 4, gap 0, radius 8 | change, but see the warning below |
| Chip/Printer+Spool | 28 high, radius 4 | `chip` | 26 high | change, but see the warning below |
| Chat/Reply Choice | 28 high, padding 0/12 | `replyChip` | 28, 12 | same |
| Field/Number, Select, Form Row | 26 high, radius 4 | `field`, `select`, `formRow` | 26 | same |
| Field/Search | 38 high, padding 8/10 | not checked | | compare |
| Segmented Control | 30 high, padding 2, radius 4 | not checked | | compare |
| Tooltip | 24 high, padding 4/8, radius 4 | not checked | | compare |
| Swatch | 24, radius 4 | `swatch` | 24, 4 | same |
| Status Dot | 8 | `statusDot` | 8 | same |
| Progress | 4 high | `progress` | 4 | same |
| Tool Panel | padding 12, gap 8, radius 8 | `toolPanel` | padding 12 | same |
| Sheet | padding 24, gap 16, radius 12 | not checked | | compare |

Finish the "not checked" rows before changing anything, so Kenneth sees the
whole list at once.

## Warning: Kenneth rejected the Figma header menu sizes once before

On 2026-09-07 Kenneth reverted the header printer/filament chip and its menu
from Figma's sizes back to the current ones (commit "Revert my header menu
restyling: it looked worse and I could not explain why", on `jusprin-newui`).
The values he kept then: chip 26 high, menu rows 32 high with radius 4 and a
4 px side inset, popover padding 4 with no gap between rows. Figma's values
(chip 28, rows 36 full width, padding 8, gap 2) are exactly what he rejected.

His 2026-10-19 ruling says the design system wins, but it was made about the
Agent chat composer, not with that revert in front of him. Before changing the
chip, Menu/Row or Menu/Popover tokens, show Kenneth both versions side by side
(a picture of the header menu at each size) and ask which one he wants. If he
keeps the code's values, the fix goes the other way: change Figma, then
re-sync the artifact.

## How to do it

1. Work in a new worktree off `jusprin-newui`. Do not use another session's
   worktree.
2. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` ("Writing UI code") and the
   guard tests: `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` (native) and
   `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` (Agent pages).
3. For each change: update the token, update the guard test so it expects the
   new value, and prove the guard fails first (set the old value back, see it
   fail, restore from a saved copy, never with `git checkout`).
4. Rebuild the Agent page bundles and the app, and check every screen that
   uses a changed token in light and dark: the header chip and its menu, the
   Agent chat (composer, reply chips, tool activity), Home, the printer
   dialog, and the settings forms. Capture pictures for Kenneth.
5. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any file
   outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`.
6. Commit only when Kenneth asks.

## Related work

The composer redesign (`handoff-composer-redesign.md`, worktree
`JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign`) needs the new Button/Icon, Menu/Row and
Menu/Popover sizes. It adds one new token group, `component.composer`
(padding 8, gap 4, inputPadding 4, maxLines 8), which is not yet in Figma.
Coordinate so the two changes do not edit the same lines of the token file at
the same time.

Leave this file untracked. Do not commit it or add it to any ignore file.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

159:## Writing UI code
160-
161-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
162-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
163-the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
164-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
165-
166-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
167-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
168-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
169-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
170-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
171-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
172-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
173-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
174-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
175-2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
176-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
177-   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
178-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
179-   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
180-   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
181-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
182-3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
183-   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
184-   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
185-4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
186-   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
187-   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
188-5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
189-   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
190-   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
191-   token file records what stayed.
192-6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
193-   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
194-   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
195-   not that the result looks right.
196-7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
197-   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
198-   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
199-   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
200-
201-## Runtime application in the native app
202-
203-The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
204-three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
205-color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
206-three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
207-
208-1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
209-   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
210-   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
211-     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
212-     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
213-     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
214-     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
215-     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
216-     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
217-     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
218-     fonts.
219-   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as

content.content:
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
  type: feedback

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
  type: project

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
  type: feedback

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.
